It solves the problem that standard arithmetic coders buffer bits into byte-sized units, making individual symbols or small groups of symbols inaccessible without decoding the entire preceding stream [S1].

The claim states that the evidence supports the assertion that the described technique solves the problem of standard arithmetic coders buffering bits into byte-sized units, which makes individual symbols inaccessible without decoding the preceding stream. Source [S1] explicitly states: 'The arithmetic coder we have adopted uses the byte as information unit... The string of bits... is temporarily stored into a buffer... Each coding unit thus represents a set of symbols, which cannot be accessed (i.e., decoded) independently.' It further explains that the proposed technique (partitioning into disjoint segments) is necessary to allow independent access, thereby solving this specific problem. The claim accurately reflects the problem description and the solution's purpose as detailed in the source.
